paperTitle: O-Level Basic Band — Practice 10: The Locked Door
provenanceNote: NOT STUDENT-FACING. Basic band. Original narrative written for the morning-quiz bank; NOT from any past exam paper. Short passage (~230 words, everyday vocabulary), 2 short-answer + 3 MCQ. Most marks reachable by choosing — typed items run a 64% blank rate in the weakest cohort.

sections.instruction: Read the story below and answer the questions that follow. [2 marks]. Write short answers.
sections.passage:
Paragraph 1
I forgot my keys on a Tuesday. I only found out at four o'clock, standing outside our flat.

Paragraph 2
My mother finishes work at seven. My father was in Malaysia for three days. I had no phone credit.

Paragraph 3
I sat on the stairs. After twenty minutes my neighbour, Mrs Lim, opened her door and looked at me.

Paragraph 4
She is seventy-eight and does not talk much. In four years we had said good morning and nothing else.

Paragraph 5
She did not ask what was wrong. She said, 'Come,' and went back inside, leaving her door open.

Paragraph 6
Her flat smelled of ginger. She gave me a bowl of soup and turned on the television. We watched a programme about fishing that neither of us was interested in. She did not talk. I did not talk. It was not uncomfortable. On her wall there was one photograph of a young man in a school uniform. I did not ask who he was.

Paragraph 7
At seven my mother came up the stairs calling my name. Mrs Lim opened the door before she could knock.

Paragraph 8
My mother tried to thank her. Mrs Lim said the soup would have been thrown away anyway.

Paragraph 9
That was not true. I had watched her make it.

questions.stem: Q3. In Paragraph 4, what do we learn about the writer and Mrs Lim? [1]

options.text: They had been close for four years.
They had barely spoken before that day.
They had argued in the past.
Mrs Lim was a relative of the family.

questions.stem: Q4. In Paragraph 5, why did Mrs Lim not ask what was wrong? [1]

options.text: She helped first and left the explaining until later.
She already knew what had happened.

questions.stem: Q5. Why does the writer end with 'That was not true'? [1]

options.text: Mrs Lim made the soup on purpose, so her excuse hid her kindness.
Mrs Lim had lied about who cooked the soup.
The writer's mother did not believe the story.
